newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close higher, led by Electricidad.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close higher, led by Electricidad.

text.p: Shares on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed higher in strong trade, led by benchmark stock Electricidad de Caracas, brokers said.
Electricidad climbed 12.00 bolivars to close at 537.50 bolivars, as investors bet on the government approving an increase in electricity tariffs shortly, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index rose 1.01 percent to 6,680.28 as 28 stocks rose, 10 slipped and eight closed flat.
"The exchange closed higher largely due to Electrcidad de Caracas," independent stocks analyst Luis Lolet said.
Interest in Electricidad sparked an active trading session with 1,060 trades for 4.875 billion bolivars ($10.4 billion).
Brokers said the market was looking "stronger" and noted renewed interest from foreign investors.
Among heavily traded stocks, market leaders telephone company CANTV rose 0.50 bolivar to 2100.50 bolivars and steel company Sivensa closed up 4.95 bolivars at 324.00 bolivars.
